title: Chapter 31. Nagari Padas — V: the "Narahari" padas of GPT (sect. 3.2, nos. 119, 124–145): the townswomen's dreams
html:
On what nagari-bhava is, the position of the tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) and the rules of translation, see the introductory note to the section of nagari padas in chapter 27; on the two poets named Narahari (Narahari Sarakara and Narahari Chakravarti) and on the attribution labels ("probably Sarakara", "probably Chakravarti", "not established"), see the introductory note to the "Narahari" appendix in chapter 17.

1. Narahari — "ghumaka-ghore bhora śacīnandana…" (GPT1 p. 205, no. 119; GCC 2.13)

Gaura asleep. At the end of the night Shachi's son, deep in sleep, as if immersed in a sleep of long ago in the kunja, softly says: "Wake, crown-jewel of women, beautiful one! Without the song of your words My hearing has no joy; open your eyes, give Me a smile; rise — I Myself will adorn you." This is not a townswoman's speech: GPT placed the pada in the section of nagari padas, but in GCC it stands in the account of the last part of the Lord's night. Raga lalita. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 2, pada 13.1

ঘুমক-ঘোরে ভোর শচীনন্দন কো সমুঝব তছু প্রেমবিলাস ।
পুরব-নিকুঞ্জে শয়নে জনু নিমগন বোলত ঐছন মধুর মৃদু ভাষ ॥

ghumaka-ghore bhora śacīnandana ko samujhaba tachu premabilāsa |
puraba-nikuñje śayane janu nimagana bolata aichana madhura mṛdu bhāṣa ||

ghumaka-ghore bhora — overcome by deep sleep; śacīnandana — Shachi's son; ko samujhaba — who will fathom; tachu premabilāsa — His play of prema; puraba-nikuñje śayane — in sleep in the kunja of old; janu nimagana — as if immersed; bolata aichana — speaks thus; madhura mṛdu bhāṣa — in sweet soft words

1.1Shachi's son, held by deep sleep — who can fathom His play of prema? — as if immersed in a sleep of long ago in the kunja, speaks thus, sweetly and softly:

জাগ জাগ রমণীশিরোমণি সুন্দরি কতহি ঘুমায়সি রজনীক শেষ ।
তব বচনামৃত-সঙ্গীত পান বিনু চঞ্চল শ্রবণ রহিত সুখলেশ ॥

jāga jāga ramaṇīśiromaṇi sundari katahi ghumāyasi rajanīka śeṣa |
taba bacanāmṛta-saṅgīta pāna binu cañcala śrabaṇa rahita sukhaleśa ||

jāga jāga — wake, wake; ramaṇīśiromaṇi sundari — crown-jewel of women, beautiful one; katahi ghumāyasi — how long you sleep; rajanīka śeṣa — at the end of the night; taba bacanāmṛta-saṅgīta — the song of the nectar of your words; pāna binu — without drinking; cañcala śrabaṇa — restless hearing; rahita sukhaleśa — bereft of the least joy

1.2"Wake, wake, crown-jewel of women, beautiful one — how long will you sleep at the end of the night? Without drinking the song of the nectar of your words, My restless hearing is bereft of the least joy.

মুদ্রিত ত্যজি তরল-নয়নাঞ্চলে ললিত ভঙ্গী করি মন মান ।
মম মন বন্ধ নিশঙ্ক কহই তোহে হাসি রভস মোহে দেহ দান ॥

mudrita tyaji tarala-nayanāñcale lalita bhaṅgī kari mana māna |
mama mana bandha niśaṅka kahai tohe hāsi rabhasa mohe deha dāna ||

mudrita tyaji — leaving the closed (eyelids); tarala-nayanāñcale — with the tremulous corners of the eyes; lalita bhaṅgī kari — with a graceful movement; mana māna — honour (sense unclear; GCC "kara sammāna" — do honour); mama mana bandha — My heart is bound (GCC: in pledge); niśaṅka kahai — I say without fear; tohe hāsi — you, smiling; rabhasa mohe deha dāna — give Me joy

1.3Leave your closed eyelids: with the tremulous corners of your eyes, with a graceful movement, do Me honour. My heart is bound — I say it without fear: smile and give Me joy.

মঝু অভিলাষ সমুঝি উঠি বৈঠহ নিজকরে বেশ বিরচব তোহারি ।
ইহ বিধি কহত নরহরি পহুঁ বহুরি নিগদত কখন বিশারি ॥

majhu abhilāṣa samujhi uṭhi baiṭhaha nijakare beśa biracaba tohāri |
iha bidhi kahata narahari pahum̐ bahuri nigadata kakhana biśāri ||

majhu abhilāṣa samujhi — understanding My wish; uṭhi baiṭhaha — rise and sit up; nijakare — with My own hands; beśa biracaba tohāri — I will adorn you; iha bidhi kahata — thus He speaks; narahari pahum̐ — Narahari's Lord; bahuri nigadata — says again; kakhana biśāri — lost to Himself (lit. "forgetting when"; GCC: "forgetting what is said")

1.4Understand My wish — rise and sit up: with My own hands I will adorn you." So speaks Narahari's Lord — and says it again, lost to Himself.2

no. 119 (catalogue: NG-098). GCC — kirana 2, pada 13 (ed. 1947, p. 30; scan PDF p. 35), "lalita-rāga". The second kirana of GCC describes the last part of the Lord's night: the bedchamber, the bees flying into the house, the birds that wake Him at dawn; in the next pada (GCC 2.14, not taken into GPT) these words spoken in sleep are heard by Gadadhara Pandita, who wakes and then keeps watch by Gaura's bed (2.15–2.16). Thus in the author Gaura in sleep speaks the words of Krishna waking Radha in the kunja at the end of the night (cf. the padas on the waking of Radha and Krishna, nishanta-lila): this is a remembrance of Vraja, not nagari-bhava; on Gadadhara as the embodiment of Radha's bhava in Gaura-lila — GGD. The pada is in Vrajabuli (tachu, mohe, tohe, majhu). B. The pada stands in the GPT section of nagari padas — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). meeting), a more explicit reading; the GPT text is translated. 1.3: "do Me honour" — after the GCC reading "kari kara sammāna" (GPT: "kari mana māna", sense unclear); "My heart is bound" — GPT "mana mana bandha" (probably a misprint for GCC "mama mana bandhaka" — "My heart is in pledge [to you]"); "give Me joy" (GPT "rabhasa") — GCC "give Me the jewel of a smile" (hāsi ratana). 1.4: "says it again, lost to Himself" (GPT "bahuri nigadata kakhana biśāri"; GCC "bahu binigadata kathana bisāri" — "speaks much, forgetting what He says") — the sense of the last words is conjectural.

2. Narahari — "mora pati ati sujana sajani…" (GPT1 pp. 207–208, no. 124; GCC 7.29)

Nagari-bhava. A townswoman tells her friend: yesterday her husband, alone with his father, said that Nimai Pandita has the power of God, has mastered His senses, is righteous, merciful to wicked people and full of the joy of kirtana; therefore the young wives should not be forbidden to see Him — His darshan destroys all that is inauspicious; as in Vraja Krishna was not recognised by the brahmanas but by their wives, so it is here. Hearing this she rejoiced, and when Gaura passed along the street with Gadadhara, Nityananda and His companions, she went out and gazed on Him to her heart's content: the other women were held back by their mothers-in-law, but no one held her back. Raga "yatharaga". Attribution: probably Chakravarti — GCC, kirana 7, pada 29.3

মোর পতি অতি সুজন সজনি শুন লো তাহার রীতি ।
গতদিন তেঁই বিরলে বসিয়া কহয়ে পিতার প্রতি ॥

mora pati ati sujana sajani śuna lo tāhāra rīti |
gatadina tem̐i birale basiyā kahaye pitāra prati ||

mora pati — my husband; ati sujana — a very good man; sajani — friend; śuna lo — do listen; tāhāra rīti — his ways; gatadina — yesterday; tem̐i — he; birale basiyā — sitting alone; kahaye pitāra prati — says to his father

2.1"My husband, friend, is a very good man: listen to what he is like. Yesterday, sitting alone with his father, he said to him:

নদীয়া নগরে নিমাই পণ্ডিত ঈশ্বর-শকতি তার ।
কেবা সিরজিল না জানি এরূপ গুণের নাহিক পার ॥

nadīyā nagare nimāi paṇḍita īśvara-śakati tāra |
kebā sirajila nā jāni erūpa guṇera nāhika pāra ||

nadīyā nagare — in the town of Nadia; nimāi paṇḍita — Nimai Pandita; īśvara-śakati tāra — in Him is the power of God; kebā sirajila — who created; nā jāni — I do not know; erūpa — such a one; guṇera nāhika pāra — no end to His virtues

2.2'In the town of Nadia is Nimai Pandita: in Him is the power of God. Who created such a wonder I do not know; there is no end to His virtues.

হেন জিতেন্দ্রিয় ধার্মিক কখন না দেখি আপন আঁখে ।
দুর্মতি-জনের প্রতি অতি দয়া ভাসয়ে কীর্তনসুখে ॥

hena jitendriya dhārmika kakhana nā dekhi āpana ām̐khe |
durmati-janera prati ati dayā bhāsaye kīrtanasukhe ||

hena — such; jitendriya — master of the senses; dhārmika — righteous; kakhana nā dekhi — I have never seen; āpana ām̐khe — with my own eyes; durmati-janera prati — towards wicked people; ati dayā — great mercy; bhāsaye kīrtanasukhe — floats in the joy of kirtana

2.3One so master of His senses and so righteous I have never seen with my own eyes. To wicked people He is boundlessly merciful; He floats in the joy of kirtana.

তাহে বলি নিজ বধূগণে কভু ভুলি না নিষেধ তুমি ।
তার দরশনে অশুভ বিনাশে নিশ্চয় জানিয়ে আমি ॥

tāhe bali nija badhūgaṇe kabhu bhuli nā niṣedha tumi |
tāra daraśane aśubha bināśe niścaya jāniye āmi ||

tāhe bali — therefore I say; nija badhūgaṇe — your daughters-in-law; kabhu bhuli nā niṣedha tumi — never, even by oversight, forbid; tāra daraśane — by His darshan; aśubha bināśe — the inauspicious perishes; niścaya jāniye āmi — I know for certain

2.4Therefore I say: never, not even by oversight, forbid your daughters-in-law [to go to Him]. I know for certain: by His darshan all that is inauspicious perishes.

ভাগ্যবতী সব বহু কি কহব অধিক কহিতে নারি ।
তাহে ধন্য এই নারী-জনমের বালাই লইয়া মরি ॥

bhāgyabatī saba bahu ki kahaba adhika kahite nāri |
tāhe dhanya ei nārī-janamera bālāi laiyā mari ||

bhāgyabatī saba bahu — fortunate are all the young wives (bahu = vadhū); ki kahaba adhika — what more shall I say; kahite nāri — I cannot express it; tāhe dhanya — therefore blessed; ei nārī-janamera — this birth as a woman; bālāi laiyā mari — I take upon myself its ills

2.5Fortunate are all our young wives — what more can I say? I cannot even express it. Therefore blessed is this birth as a woman — I take upon myself all its ills.

মিছা অভিমানে মাতি রাতি দিন রহিএ অন্ধের পারা ।
নদীয়ার মাঝে হেন অপরূপ চিনিতে নারিয়ে মোরা ॥

michā abhimāne māti rāti dina rahie andhera pārā |
nadīyāra mājhe hena aparūpa cinite nāriye morā ||

michā abhimāne māti — drunk with false pride; rāti dina — night and day; rahie andhera pārā — we live like the blind; nadīyāra mājhe — in the midst of Nadia; hena aparūpa — such a Wonder; cinite nāriye morā — we cannot recognise

2.6But we, drunk with false pride, live day and night like the blind: such a Wonder in the midst of Nadia — and we cannot recognise Him.

ব্রজে ব্রজনাথে দ্বিজে না জানিল পাইল দ্বিজের নারী ।
সেইরূপ এথা ইথে না সন্দেহ বুঝিনু বিচার করি ॥

braje brajanāthe dvije nā jānila pāila dvijera nārī |
seirūpa ethā ithe nā sandeha bujhinu bicāra kari ||

braje — in Vraja; brajanāthe — the Lord of Vraja; dvije nā jānila — the brahmanas did not know; pāila dvijera nārī — the brahmanas' wives attained; seirūpa ethā — so it is here; ithe nā sandeha — no doubt in this; bujhinu bicāra kari — I have understood, reflecting

2.7In Vraja the brahmanas did not know the Lord of Vraja — the brahmanas' wives attained Him. So it is here, there is no doubt of it — I have understood, having reflected.'4

এইরূপ পিতাপুত্র দুঁহে কথা কহয়ে অনেক মতে ।
আড়ে থাকি তাহা শুনিয়া শুনিয়া হনু উলসিত চিতে ॥

eirūpa pitāputra dum̐he kathā kahaye aneka mate |
āṛe thāki tāhā śuniyā śuniyā hanu ulasita cite ||

eirūpa — thus; pitā-putra dum̐he — father and son both; kathā kahaye aneka mate — talk in many ways; āṛe thāki — staying hidden; tāhā śuniyā śuniyā — listening and listening to it; hanu ulasita cite — I rejoiced in heart

2.8So father and son talked long in many ways; hidden nearby, I listened and listened — and my heart rejoiced.

মনে হৈল হেন বেলে যদি গোরাচাঁদেরে দেখিতে পাতু ।
নয়নের কোণে এ সব কাহিনী তাহারে কহিয়ে দিতু ॥

mane haila hena bele yadi gorācām̐dere dekhite pātu |
nayanera koṇe e saba kāhinī tāhāre kahiye ditu ||

mane haila — I thought; hena bele — at this hour; yadi gorācām̐dere dekhite pātu — if I could see Gorachand; nayanera koṇe — with the corners of my eyes; e saba kāhinī — all this story; tāhāre kahiye ditu — I would tell Him

2.9I thought: if only I could see Gorachand right now — with the corners of my eyes I would tell Him all this.

এইকালে পাড়া পানে ঘন ঘন উঠিল আনন্দ-ধ্বনি ।
তরাতরি পথে দাঁড়াইনু গিয়া গৌরগমন জানি ॥

eikāle pāṛā pāne ghana ghana uṭhila ānanda-dhvani |
tarātari pathe dām̐ṛāinu giyā gauragamana jāni ||

eikāle — at this time; pāṛā pāne — from the direction of our quarter; ghana ghana — again and again; uṭhila ānanda-dhvani — joyful cries rose; tarātari — in haste; pathe dām̐ṛāinu giyā — I went and stood by the road; gauragamana jāni — knowing Gaura was coming

2.10Just then, from the direction of our quarter, joyful cries rose again and again; knowing that Gaura was coming, I hurried out and stood by the road.

দূরে থাকি আঁখি ভরি নিরখিনু কিবা অপরূপ শোভা ।
ঝলমল করে চারিদিকে হেম জিনিয়া অঙ্গের আভা ॥

dūre thāki ām̐khi bhari nirakhinu kibā aparūpa śobhā |
jhalamala kare cāridike hema jiniyā aṅgera ābhā ||

dūre thāki — from afar; ām̐khi bhari — to my eyes' content; nirakhinu — I gazed; kibā aparūpa śobhā — what wondrous beauty; jhalamala kare — blazes; cāridike — in every direction; hema jiniyā — outshining gold; aṅgera ābhā — the radiance of His body

2.11From afar I gazed my fill — what wondrous beauty! The radiance of His body, outshining gold, blazes in every direction.

তার বামে গদাধর নিত্যানন্দ দক্ষিণে আনন্দরাশি ।
চারিপাশে আর পরিকর তারা নিরখে ও মুখশশী ॥

tāra bāme gadādhara nityānanda dakṣiṇe ānandarāśi |
cāripāśe āra parikara tārā nirakhe o mukhaśaśī ||

tāra bāme — on His left; gadādhara — Gadadhara; nityānanda dakṣiṇe — on His right Nityananda; ānandarāśi — bliss itself; cāripāśe — all around; āra parikara tārā — the other companions; nirakhe o mukhaśaśī — gaze at that moon of a face

2.12On His left is Gadadhara, on His right Nityananda, bliss itself; all around are His other companions: all gaze at that moon of a face.

নিজগণ সঙ্গে রসিকশেখর আইসে রসের ভরে ।
সে চাহনি চারু হেরিয়া এমন কে আছে পরাণ ধরে ॥

nijagaṇa saṅge rasikaśekhara āise rasera bhare |
se cāhani cāru heriyā emana ke āche parāṇa dhare ||

nijagaṇa saṅge — with His own companions; rasikaśekhara — the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa; āise rasera bhare — comes overflowing with rasa; se cāhani cāru heriyā — seeing that lovely glance; emana ke āche — who is there; parāṇa dhare — who keeps hold of her heart (lit. "life")

2.13With His own companions the Crown of connoisseurs of rasa comes, overflowing with rasa; who, seeing that lovely glance, can keep hold of her heart?

হাসি হাসি কথা-ছলে সুধারাশি বরিখে নদ্যার চাঁদ ।
অঙ্গ-ভঙ্গী ভারি ভুলালে ভুবন যেন সে মদনফাঁদ ॥

hāsi hāsi kathā-chale sudhārāśi barikhe nadyāra cām̐da |
aṅga-bhaṅgī bhāri bhulāle bhubana yena se madanaphām̐da ||

hāsi hāsi — smiling; kathā-chale — as if in talk; sudhārāśi barikhe — showers streams of nectar; nadyāra cām̐da — the Moon of Nadia; aṅga-bhaṅgī bhāri — the grace of His form; bhulāle bhubana — captivated the world; yena se madana-phām̐da — like the snare of Madana

2.14Smiling, as if in conversation, the Moon of Nadia showers streams of nectar; the grace of His form has captivated the world — like the snare of Madana.

প্রাণনাথ গতি জানি পাড়াবাসী যুবতী আসিয়ে ধাঞা ।
তা সবার শাশুড়ী ননদী দারুণ নিবারি অনেক কৈঞা ॥

prāṇanātha gati jāni pāṛābāsī yubatī āsiye dhāñā |
tā sabāra śāśuṛī nanadī dāruṇa nibāri aneka kaiñā ||

prāṇanātha gati jāni — knowing the Lord of their life was coming; pāṛābāsī yubatī — the young women of the quarter; āsiye dhāñā — came running; tā sabāra śāśuṛī nanadī — their mothers-in-law and sisters-in-law; dāruṇa — harsh; nibāri aneka kaiñā — held them back with many words

2.15Knowing that the Lord of their life was coming, the young women of our quarter came running; their harsh mothers-in-law and sisters-in-law held them back with many words.5

মোরে কেহ নাহি নিবারিল মুই পূরালু মনের সাধা ।
নরহরি কহে যার পতি অতি প্রসন্ন তার কি বাধা ॥

more keha nāhi nibārila mui pūrālu manera sādhā |
narahari kahe yāra pati ati prasanna tāra ki bādhā ||

more keha nāhi nibārila — no one held me back; mui pūrālu manera sādhā — I fulfilled my heart's desire; narahari kahe — Narahari says; yāra pati ati prasanna — whose husband is very gracious; tāra ki bādhā — what obstacle has she

2.16But no one held me back — I fulfilled my heart's desire." Narahari says: she whose husband is so gracious — what obstacles has she?

pp. 89–90; scan PDF pp. 86–87; the pada begins with the first line of p. 89 — directly after the lost pp. 81–88, see n. 18 of chapter 30). GPT nos. 124–126 are the last padas of the 7th kirana of GCC (7.29–7.31). GCC readings: "seirūpa hethā", "hema jiniyā" (2.11; GPT1 and GPT2 "hena", a misprint; translated after GCC), "āise dhāyā … nibāre aneka kaiyā" (2.15), "pāinu manera sādhā" (2.16). B. Nagari-bhava — see the introductory note to the section (chapter 27). senses (jitendriya), is merciful to the wicked — cf. in CB (Madhya) the deliverance of Jagai and Madhai and the words that the Lord's kirtana purifies even sinners. 2.7 — the story of the wives of the sacrificing brahmanas (Bhag. 10.23): the brahmana priests did not recognise Krishna and refused Him food, while their wives left everything, came to Him and received His mercy. So in this pada the rightness of the women who long to see Gaura is affirmed by a husband in conversation with his father. faithfully to the author. The townswoman herself in this pada only gazes at Gaura from afar, standing by the road.

3. Narahari — "śuna śuna sai bidhi arasika…" (GPT1 pp. 208–209, no. 125; GCC 7.30)

Nagari-bhava. GCC readings: "prabeśila adhika madana-bhare" — "entered, overflowing with Madana" (13.2; GPT "athira ānanda bhare", "trembling with joy"; the GPT text is translated), "basilena nanadinīra pālaṅka-pare" (13.2), "kara-pallave cibuka paraśe haraṣa haiyā" (13.3), "kata dūre yāi pāila, palāite nārila parāṇapiyā" (13.5), "yaubana-garabe" (13.6), "tem̐ha adhomukhe" (13.9), "parabhāte haibe kalaṅka-dhūma" (13.10). The pada is a farce: the strict sister-in-law who guards the young wife is herself "conquered" by Gaura; this is the motif running through GCC (the strict elders, on seeing Gaura, lose their severity; cf. nn. 12, 23 of chapter 30) carried to a coarse joke. Such a depiction of the Lord is precisely what the Gaudiya tradition rejects: the Lord did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi); the worship of Gaura as a nagara is an apasampradaya (Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati; introductory note, chapter 27). This is a townswoman's dream told for laughter (13.1: "what a laugh!"). witness; the last words (āśvāsite bhāṅgila ām̐khira ghuma — "as [I] began to console her, sleep left the eyes") are understood thus: the teller herself consoles her sister-in-law and at once wakes up (cf. the ending of 12.8: "I saved my life by waking up quickly"); the subject is not named in the original, and the reading "as he began to console her" is also possible.

Summary of chapter 31

The chapter continues the padas signed "Narahari" from section 3.2 of GPT. All 23 padas were found in Narahari Chakravarti's "Gaura-charita-chintamani" and checked against its scan ("probably Chakravarti" — B): no. 119 (no. 1) = GCC 2.13 — Gaura in sleep speaks the words of Krishna waking Radha (not nagari-bhava; GPT placed it in the section of nagari padas); nos. 124–125 (nos. 2–3) = GCC 7.29–7.30 — the end of the townswomen's morning tales (the husband praising Nimai Pandita; the house of Murari Gupta); nos. 126–144 (nos. 4–22) = GCC 8.2–8.20 — the 8th kirana, "the tales of dreams": at dawn the townswomen tell their friends their dreams of Gaura and then speak of their love and of good omens; no. 145 (no. 23) = GCC 9.1 — the beginning of the 9th kirana. Dreams with a direct motif of sambhoga (embrace, kiss, "He did what was in His heart") are translated exactly, without additions and without softening, each with a note: the dream is the townswoman's imagination, the Lord in His lila did not touch women and in Navadvipa did not look at them (CB, Adi), the Gaudiya tradition does not accept the worship of Gaura as a nagara (introductory note, chapter 27). Where GCC is more explicit than GPT ("drunk with Madana", "lay down" instead of "sat", the extra lines in no. 17), the GPT text is translated and the GCC reading noted.
